text: Ever stood at a bus stop, clock-watching, wondering why your ride isn't here? You just want to reach your destination, quickly and simply.
Sometimes buses arrive in bursts, then nothing. An empty one rushes past. Why can't they just come when people need them?
The naive idea: send a bus only when passengers wait. But imagine buses driving randomly! Roads would be a coral red mess of chaos.
That's the schedule's purpose. It's a signal blue system coordinating *everyone's* expectations – riders, drivers. It tells you and the bus when to be there.
The 'cost' is waiting, or a bus passing half-empty. But without the schedule, the entire network would collapse into unpredictable chaos.
So next time you glance at the timetable, remember: the schedule isn't there to annoy. It makes mass transit possible, moving millions predictably.
